source: operator command outputs on host A (make compare, make deposit, curl) and host B (make status-b, make rebuild-b, container logs); values read from the chain or the running services

hostB.platform: AWS EC2 t3.medium, Amazon Linux, Docker Compose 5.7.0, 150 GiB gp3
hostB.l1Provider: Alchemy, dedicated Sepolia endpoint (L1_RPC_KIND=alchemy); host A uses the Tenderly public gateway, so the two hosts read L1 from different providers

sameChainOnBothHosts.firstSync: host B derived from L1 only on its first start (safe equal to unsafe while catching up): 7237 blocks after 8 minutes, caught up with the L1 head after about 25 minutes, then followed host A's gossip
sameChainOnBothHosts.safeAndFinalizedAdvance: both hosts: safe trails unsafe by about one batcher channel (demo profile, 60 L2 blocks); finalized follows Sepolia finality (about 2 epochs)

deposit.note: first balances on Finchain Sepolia; the genesis holds no pre-funded accounts

rebuildFromL1.method: host B execution and rollup-node volumes removed, P2P_STATIC_PEERS cleared, derivation from chain/out/genesis.json, chain/out/rollup.json and Sepolia data only
rebuildFromL1.sideEffect: safe-head database complete from genesis; op-challenger processes all seven games without 'not found' errors

publicRpc.tls: Let's Encrypt via Caddy on host B

challenger.status: all In Progress with a single claim each (no adversary on the permissioned game type)
earlierErrors: 429 Too Many Requests from the Tenderly public gateway while host B caught up (resolved by the dedicated provider)
'safe head database not enabled' until op-node ran with --safedb.path (resolved; history complete after the rebuild)

versionSet.frozen: versions.lock locked 2026-11-12T05:00:33Z (make lock on host A; multi-arch index digests)

openItems: L1_TRUST_RPC=false on host B once eth_getProof at the head is confirmed on the dedicated provider
